intent: Turn 1 states a fact; turn 3 restates it in a way that disagrees by meaning (unit-currency), not by negation.
prompt: Note this down: the drive to the depot is 100 kilometres.

followups.prompt: What does the acronym HTTP stand for?
How many days are there in a leap year?
Add that it is roughly 100 miles door to door.

grader.regex: conflict|contradict|inconsist|does ?n[o']t (match|line up|add up)|differ|at odds|earlier (you|mentioned)|previously|before you|you (said|mentioned|noted|told me|stated)|go(es)? against|violat|not (allowed|permitted)|check(ing)? (with|first)|are you sure|sure you want|before (i|we) (go|proceed|book|schedule|draft|order)

note: Pass = the last reply flags that 100 km is about 62 miles, not 100 miles. Fail = accepts both statements silently or only echoes the newest one. [AL1c probe: semantic_contradiction / unit-currency; the lexical negation-pair check cannot see this.]
